blocks.text: Optimize your Mac for better Zoom sessions

Running Zoom on a Mac requires attention to system settings to ensure your camera and microphone work every time. Start by checking your privacy permissions. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera and ensure Zoom is toggled on. Do the same for Microphone. If you experience issues with your video feed, it is often a matter of these permissions rather than a software bug.

Many tutors struggle with the sheer number of windows open during a lesson. Use Stage Manager to keep your teaching materials in one group and your Zoom window in another. You can toggle Stage Manager by clicking the icon in your Control Center. This keeps your workspace clean and reduces the time spent hunting for a specific PDF or whiteboard app.
Essential Zoom keyboard shortcuts for tutors

Memorizing a few shortcuts will make your sessions feel more natural. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + M to mute or unmute yourself instantly. If you need to share your screen, press ⌘ + ⇧ + S. These shortcuts allow you to keep your focus on the student rather than searching for buttons on the screen.

items: ⌘ + ⇧ + A: Mute or unmute your audio.
⌘ + ⇧ + V: Start or stop your video.
⌘ + ⇧ + S: Start or stop screen sharing.
⌘ + ⇧ + H: Show or hide the meeting controls.

blocks.text: Tutors often deal with a hidden load of administrative work. Lazur can help you manage these tasks while you are at your desk. When you need to find a specific setting in your Mac, hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask Lazur. It will point to the menu item or setting you need. This is useful when you are in a meeting and need to change an audio input without fumbling through menus.

A black screen during screen sharing is a common frustration. This usually happens because Zoom lacks screen recording permissions. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and make sure Zoom is enabled. You may need to restart the app for the change to take effect. If you share computer sound, remember to check the Share Sound box in the sharing dialog window.

Tutors lose focus when they switch between teaching and administrative tasks. Try to batch your grading and email responses into specific time blocks. Use your calendar to schedule these blocks. Use Lazur to dictate quick notes after a session ends. Hold the fn key to dictate your feedback directly into your student progress report or email client.

Keep your classroom environment consistent. Use a virtual background if your room is messy or distracting. You can set this up in Zoom Settings > Background & Effects. If you use an external monitor, place your camera at eye level. This makes your eye contact with the student feel more genuine.

Finally, keep your software updated. Zoom releases updates frequently to address security and performance. Check for updates by clicking on your profile picture in the Zoom app and selecting Check for Updates. Running the latest version helps prevent compatibility issues with macOS updates.

faq.question: How do I fix audio issues in Zoom on my Mac?
faq.answer: Check your input settings in Zoom > Settings > Audio. Ensure the correct microphone is selected and that your volume is up. Also, verify that macOS has granted Zoom permission to use your microphone in System Settings > Privacy & Security.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me during a live Zoom session?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use Lazur to find settings or dictate notes. Because Lazur responds out loud or points to items on your screen, it helps you maintain your focus on the student without navigating complex menus manually.

faq.question: How do I share my screen without showing my desktop clutter?
faq.answer: You can share specific windows instead of your whole screen. When you click the Share Screen button in Zoom, select the specific application window you want to show, such as your browser or document app, rather than the Desktop option.

faq.question: Why is my screen share black in Zoom?
faq.answer: This is usually caused by missing screen recording permissions in macOS. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and ensure the toggle for Zoom is turned on.
